served.stem:
Predict the MAJOR product of the following reaction:

(E)-3-hexene is treated with one equivalent of mCPBA.

Which structure is the major product?
served.bankWhy: Epoxidation is syn/stereospecific, so E (trans) alkene gives trans-3,4-epoxyhexane, the (R,R)/(S,S) chiral pair. Two-concept (stereospecific syn + trans recognition).

answer.line: mCPBA hands one oxygen to one face in a single step, so nothing rotates: the trans alkene becomes the trans epoxide.

steps: Read the alkene: trans-3-hexene, its two ethyl groups on opposite sides of the C=C.
mCPBA delivers one O to one face in one step, with no cation and no rotation. The ethyls stay put.
Pick the epoxide that shows them trans, one ethyl toward you and one away. mCPBA makes both mirror images; one is drawn.

choices.note: Both ethyls on one face is the cis epoxide, a meso compound and a diastereomer of the key. It comes from cis-3-hexene.
Right ring, right atoms, but the reaction fixes the ethyls trans, and only one choice shows that. Pick the drawing that carries the stereochemistry.
A diol comes from OsO4 or KMnO4, or from opening the epoxide with aqueous acid. One equivalent of mCPBA stops at the epoxide.
This meso diol is what you get after aqueous acid opens the trans epoxide, anti across the ring. mCPBA alone does not open it.
Trans in, trans out: one ethyl on each face of the ring.

student.lockIt: Epoxidation is syn and concerted, so the alkene geometry carries over: trans gives trans, cis gives cis.

playWith.label: Tree, alkene additions: the trans-2-butene tab, compare a syn reagent with an anti reagent on a trans alkene

visual.note: One step, one face: the ethyls keep their trans relationship. mCPBA makes both mirror images; one is drawn.

visual.alt: Trans-3-hexene, its two ethyl groups on opposite sides of the C=C, reacts with one equivalent of mCPBA to give trans-2,3-diethyloxirane, drawn with the two ethyls on opposite faces and the new ring oxygen outlined.
visual.caption: The ethyls start on opposite sides and end on opposite faces. One step, no rotation.
